Defense Mechanisms

where the feeling goes · mature or immatureWhere did the feeling go?

Practice
  1. A nurse is criticized harshly by her supervisor and says nothing in reply That evening she snaps at her teenage son over a small mess in the kitchen She later admits her anger was really at the supervisor → Displacement → Anger at a superior redirected onto a safer target is displacement; passive aggression stays aimed at the source, and projection attributes the feeling to someone else
  2. A married man privately attracted to a coworker tells no one about it He repeatedly accuses his wife of flirting with other men She has given no cause for suspicion; he denies any interest in anyone else → Projection → Attributing his own unacceptable attraction to his wife is projection; displacement would redirect a feeling to a neutral target, and reaction formation would flip it
  3. A 16-year-old has frequent angry outbursts toward his strict father He joins the wrestling team and pours the anger into training His grades and mood improve, and he now competes at the state level → Sublimation → Channeling aggression into an acceptable activity is sublimation, a mature defense; reaction formation would show the opposite feeling, and acting out is impulsive action
  4. A medical student learns the night before an exam that her grandmother was hospitalized She decides to set the worry aside until the exam is over Afterward she calls her family and talks openly about her fears → Suppression → Deliberately and temporarily setting a feeling aside is suppression, a mature defense; repression is involuntary, and denial treats the reality as absent
  5. A 52-year-old man just diagnosed with lung cancer meets his oncologist He asks only about survival statistics and staging systems When asked how he feels about the news, he cites published response rates instead → Intellectualization → Retreating into facts to avoid distressing feelings is intellectualization; rationalization justifies an action, and denial would reject the diagnosis
Pairs with Cluster B Personality Disorders: splitting in borderline personality disorder.
Transferable rule

Find the source of the feeling and where it went; the destination names the defense.
